title: Alignment-Aware 3D Point Cloud Anomaly Detection with Adversarial Normalizing Flows
content: Detecting morphological anomalies in 3D point clouds remains challenging when distinguishing abnormal geometric patterns from pose variability, residual registration errors, sampling noise, and normal inter-subject anatomical variation. This problem is particularly relevant in translational neuroimaging, where pathological shape changes may be subtle, spatially localized, and difficult to annotate exhaustively. To address this limitation, this work proposes an unsupervised alignment-aware framework for 3D point-cloud anomaly detection, termed AdvFlow3D-AD, that combines optimized geometric normalization with probabilistic latent-space modeling. The framework follows a two-stage design. First, Fast Global Registration, followed by multi-scale Iterative Closest Point refinement, reduces the spatial mismatch between normal reference shapes and test point clouds. Second, an adversarially regularized normalizing flow is trained exclusively on aligned normal point coordinates to map 3D morphology into a Gaussian latent space. Point-level anomaly scores are then computed from distances to the learned normal latent support, while adaptive percentile-based thresholds provide calibrated point-level and object-level decisions under different deformation regimes. The proposed framework was evaluated on the Real3D-AD and Anomaly ShapeNet3D benchmarks and further explored in a neurodevelopmental brain-shape dataset involving pediatric cases with perinatal asphyxia. On the public benchmarks, AdvFlow3D-AD achieved competitive performance, including a point-level AUROC of 0.747 on Real3D-AD and an object-level AUROC of 0.816 on Anomaly ShapeNet3D. In the neurodevelopmental case study, the detected anomaly maps were reviewed by neuroradiology experts and localized to anatomically plausible hippocampal and cerebellar regions. These findings suggest that alignment-aware probabilistic anomaly detection supports interpretable 3D morphological analysis and knowledge extraction when abnormal labels are scarce.
